Founded in 2018 and headquartered in the Boston, Massachusetts area, the company deploys into existing warehouses in days with no WMS integration and counts UPS among its customers. Pickle Robot exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sereact
providers.description: Sereact GmbH is a Stuttgart, Germany based physical-AI company building intelligent robotic systems for warehouse and fulfillment automation. Its "Cortex" platform pairs a Vision Language Action Model (VLAM) with robot control so robots can pick, place, sort, induct, and inspect diverse items in production without task-specific retraining, running across 50+ deployments in Europe and the US. Products include Pick-and-Place, Putwall, Induction, Bin Handling, Returns Handling, and the Lens perception system. Backed by Creandum and Point Nine; announced a $110M Series B. Sereact does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — an internal api.sereact.ai host exists but is a placeholder. This profile captures the company identity and public web/GitHub surface.

providers.name: SilverRail
providers.description: SilverRail Technologies is a rail technology company that powers global rail ecommerce and distribution. Its platform spans journey planning, ticketing, and onboard information, aiming to transform the rail experience for travelers while making rail retail easier and more profitable for operators, travel agencies, and distributors. SilverRail connects rail carriers and sellers so rail inventory can be searched, booked, and ticketed across markets. The company was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel and Canaan Partners. As of this enrichment pass SilverRail runs a corporate marketing site (Next.js) but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery documents; its API and distribution capabilities appear to be delivered through partner/enterprise integration rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Zauber
providers.description: Zauber is an AI agent platform purpose-built for sea and air freight forwarding operations. Freight forwarders describe their processes in plain language and Zauber's AI agents execute them consistently across global operations, automating rate and booking workflows with exception handling, deploying global workflows with local execution, and giving operators real-time operational visibility into conversion rates, response times, and exception patterns. The platform integrates with existing systems including Office 365, CargoWise One, carrier portals, and proprietary tooling. Zauber is a portfolio company of Point Nine. No public API, developer portal, or developer documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company's identity and security posture.

providers.name: APX
providers.description: APX (APX Logistics Solutions) is a Southeast Asian less-than-truckload (LTL) digital logistics platform headquartered in Bangkok, with operations in Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore. It positions itself as the region's first LTL digital logistics provider, offering domestic and cross-border shipping, international sea and air freight, customs brokerage, warehousing and distribution, project logistics, and heavy-lift/breakbulk services. Its proprietary technology platform provides online shipment booking, real-time tracking with ETA notifications, digital proof-of-delivery, AI-assisted route optimization, a driver app, and analytics dashboards including CO2/ESG reporting. APX is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass APX publishes no first-party public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; shipment tracking is currently integrable only via third-party aggregators.

providers.name: Kakehashi
providers.description: Kakehashi is a Japanese healthcare technology company digitally transforming the country's roughly 60,000 community pharmacies, a traditionally paper-based sector. Its flagship cloud platform Musubi provides electronic medication history, automated dispensing records, and personalized patient guidance, and is used by more than 14,000 pharmacies across Japan. The product suite extends to Musubi Insight (pharmacy management analytics), Pocket Musubi (patient follow-up app), Musubi AI Stock Management (machine-learning demand forecasting and inventory optimization), and Pharmarket. Kakehashi is backed by investors including 500 Global and Goldman Sachs. No public developer API or platform is currently published.

providers.name: Transfix
providers.description: Transfix is a New York-based freight technology company that, since divesting its brokerage operation to NFI Industries in June 2024, operates as a SaaS and data company providing AI-powered Transportation Management System (TMS) software to freight brokers, third-party logistics providers (3PLs), shippers, and carriers across the United States. The Transfix TMS unifies pricing, planning, execution, and billing in a single platform, with feature areas covering Smart Pricing and Quoting, RFP Management and Collaboration, Coverage and Carrier Management, Streamlined Scheduling, Operations and Automation, Invoicing and Payments, and Reporting and Insights. Core AI capabilities include the Custom Rate Prediction Suite for spot and contract pricing across Dry Van, Reefer, and Flatbed equipment, and the RFP Workflow with a Smart Upload feature that structures bid data from heterogeneous file formats. Transfix markets integrations with existing TMS, carrier networks, and data sources, and references freight API integrations in marketing material, but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or open-source repositories. NFI Industries is the platform's anchor third-party customer following the brokerage divestiture.

providers.name: Werner Enterprises
providers.description: Werner Enterprises is a leading transportation and logistics company providing truckload transportation services, logistics solutions, and supply chain management throughout North America. Founded in 1956 and headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, Werner operates one of the largest fleets in the United States and offers freight brokerage, dedicated carriage, intermodal, and final-mile delivery services through its Werner Bridge℠ digital freight platform.

providers.name: Whole Surplus
providers.description: Whole Surplus (now operating as Fazla) is a Turkish technology-based waste management and circular-economy company backed by Techstars. It prevents waste at its source and recovers surplus products back into the circular economy with maximum environmental, social, and economic benefit across the entire supply chain from producers to consumers. Its platform combines an AI-powered analysis tool that identifies the optimal recovery path for each product with services including Fazla Market (discounted resale), donations to food banks, animal-feed conversion, recycling, a smart-scale detection system, and sustainability consultancy. Fazla is the first B Corp certified waste-management company in Turkey and is supported by the UN Development Programme (UNDP). The company operates a customer web application (app.fazla.com) but publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: BuyBuddy
providers.description: BuyBuddy is an AI-powered retail merchandising platform positioned as an "AI Merchandiser that tracks, thinks & acts for you." It automates in-store operations for retailers and brands, including planogram compliance and shelf monitoring via computer vision, stockout prevention, product placement optimization, dynamic pricing and promotions, demand forecasting, store transfers, and shopper-behavior analysis through smart tags. BuyBuddy is a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; at time of enrichment BuyBuddy publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or specification surface, so this remains a company-level profile.

providers.name: Locusrobotics
providers.description: Locus Robotics is a warehouse automation company that builds autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and the LocusONE platform, a data-science-driven system for enterprise-wide AMR deployments and warehouse performance management. Its fleet (Locus Array, Origin, and Vector robots) plus integrated software supports robots-to-goods and autonomous fulfillment across 3PL, retail, healthcare, and industrial operations. LocusONE integrates with leading WMS platforms through the LocusConnect middleware, a REST API secured with OAuth 2.0 and documented as OpenAPI 2.0 via SwaggerUI; API access is provisioned per customer rather than published as an open developer program. Locus Robotics is backed by Bond Capital and maintains an active open-source presence in the ROS (Robot Operating System) ecosystem on GitHub.

providers.name: Kiva Systems (Amazon Robotics since 2012)
providers.description: Kiva Systems was a warehouse robotics company founded in 2003 that pioneered the goods-to-person mobile fulfillment model, in which fleets of low-profile drive units lift and carry mobile storage pods to human pick stations instead of moving workers to static shelving. Amazon acquired Kiva Systems in March 2012 for approximately US$775 million and renamed it Amazon Robotics in 2015. Since the acquisition the technology has been developed exclusively for Amazon's own fulfillment and sortation network and is no longer sold to third parties. Amazon Robotics publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; amazonrobotics.com now redirects to Amazon's internal identity provider and kivasystems.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical and acquisition record in the physical-AI and warehouse-robotics space rather than as an integratable API provider. Not to be confused with AWS RoboMaker or AWS IoT RoboRunner, which are AWS product APIs.

providers.name: Universal Corporation
providers.description: Universal Corporation is a global leaf tobacco merchant and processor that selects, buys, processes, packs, stores, ships, and finances leaf tobacco for sale to manufacturers of consumer tobacco products. Operating in approximately 30 countries, Universal Corporation is the world's leading supplier of leaf tobacco, providing supply chain management, processing, and blending services. The company has developed digital platforms including MobiLeaf, a tablet-based grower management system for tobacco farmer support and crop tracking.

providers.name: Torchdental
providers.description: Torchdental (Torch Dental) is a B2B dental-supply procurement platform for independent dental practices and dental groups. It runs a web application at app.torchdental.com that lets practices order dental supplies and equipment from multiple vendors in one place, compare prices, manage recurring ordering and budgets, and streamline back-office purchasing. The company is venture backed and was surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis. As of this enrichment pass Torchdental exposes no public developer/API surface: no api/docs/developer subdomains resolve, and the application host publishes no /.well-known/ discovery documents. This profile therefore captures company identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Vend
providers.description: Vend was a cloud-based retail point-of-sale and inventory management software company founded in Auckland, New Zealand, backed by investors including Point Nine. Lightspeed announced its acquisition of Vend in March 2021 for approximately US$350 million, and the product lives on as Lightspeed Retail (X-Series). vendhq.com redirects to lightspeedhq.com/vend/, and the former Vend API is documented today at x-series-api.lightspeedhq.com. The X-Series API surface is profiled in the API Evangelist network under the Lightspeed provider, so this profile records the acquired Vend brand rather than duplicating that API.

providers.name: Captain's Eye
providers.description: Captain's Eye is a Haifa, Israel-based maritime AI company (founded 2020 by Uri Ben Dor and Doron Oizerovich, backed by Techstars) that delivers real-time video analytics software for maritime and industrial safety. Its SaaS platform connects to existing CCTV cameras, radar, and thermal sensors aboard merchant vessels, yachts, cruise ships, ports, and on-land petrochemical and energy sites, applying custom neural networks and commercial AI models to detect fires, smoke, leaks, sea pollution, missing protective gear, unauthorized access, and equipment failures. It provides real-time alerts, remote monitoring, incident documentation, and operational data collection, monitoring 5,000+ cameras and having detected 100,000+ events. Access is delivered through a private web application and mobile apps rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Jeh Aerospace
providers.description: Jeh Aerospace is a precision aerospace manufacturing company building "future factories" across the US-India corridor to supply aerostructures and aero-engine components for the commercial aerospace supply chain. From certified facilities in India spanning more than 160,000 square feet, Jeh delivers machining, sheet metal, tubes and pipes, surface treatment, structural assembly, and engineering services on time and at scale. The company is fully compliant with AS9100, ISO 9001, OEM requirements, and export regulations, and weaves a digital thread across its supplier networks for radical transparency. Jeh operates from both the US and India and is backed by General Catalyst and IndiGo Ventures.

providers.name: AI Fleet
providers.description: Aifleet (aifleet.com) is a technology-driven, full-stack trucking carrier founded in 2020 and headquartered in Austin, Texas. The company describes itself as the first full-stack, AI-driven carrier, pairing company drivers with proprietary AI algorithms and its own Transportation Management System (TMS) to optimize truck utilization, routing, load matching, fuel usage, and scheduling across the roughly $400B U.S. freight sector. Aifleet emphasizes a driver-centric model — better pay, predictable schedules, and reduced wait times — alongside shipper-facing services with proactive tracking updates and predictive ETAs. It has raised roughly $50M since founding (Series A 2021, venture round 2023, Series B 2024) from investors including Obvious Ventures, Ibex Investors, Volvo Group Venture Capital, Compound, and Heron Rock. Aifleet is a logistics service provider rather than a developer-facing API platform; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Aiperia
providers.description: Aiperia (formerly PlanerAI) is a German AI company whose SaaS platform automates demand forecasting and fresh-food supply-chain planning from production through to the end consumer. Its machine-learning models predict fresh-food demand up to 21 days ahead using around 150 external factors, then generate automated order and production suggestions for bakeries and self-service stations, food manufacturers, and supermarkets to reduce food waste and overproduction. Aiperia is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital.

providers.name: Bizongo
providers.description: Bizongo is a Mumbai-based B2B commerce and supply-chain platform founded in 2015 that digitizes procurement, vendor management, and supply-chain financing for enterprises across India, with a focus on packaging, raw materials, and made-to-order goods. It operates a SaaS-led vendor digitization stack plus an embedded-finance offering, connecting large buyers with a network of manufacturing partners. Bizongo is backed by Accel, Chiratae Ventures, B Capital, and others. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; as of this enrichment pass Bizongo publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, or /.well-known discovery surface — third-party logistics integration is offered only through carrier aggregators such as ClickPost, so most API-artifact scoring dimensions are not applicable.

providers.name: Dryft
providers.description: Dryft, Inc. is a Palo Alto, California startup building an AI operating system for manufacturing operations. The platform pairs context-aware, agent-based intelligence with mathematical optimization to mimic, optimize, and automate complex human decisions across the shop floor and supply chain. Dryft reads operational data from existing ERPs and inventory systems, identifies issues such as late items or stockouts, and autonomously recommends and executes actions like adjusting order quantities and safety stocks or following up with suppliers. The company frames this as a shift from static Enterprise Resource Planning to Enterprise Resource Automation, freeing planners to focus on strategy over administrative work. Founded in 2024 by CEO Anna-Julia Storch and CTO Leonie Freisinger, Dryft raised a $5M round led by General Catalyst with participation from Neo and Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners. Dryft does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation; this profile captures its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.
